purpose: A small, fixed set of 16 kHz WAV clips scored end to end by Full_Pipeline_Audio_Benchmark.py on every device. It is a controlled deployment benchmark, not a comprehensive speech-recognition benchmark and not a replacement for the large held-out text evaluation.

synthetic_privacy.name: synthetic privacy speech benchmark
synthetic_privacy.source: Piper TTS (MIT) reading sentences written for this project
synthetic_privacy.license: Piper is MIT. Voice models are trained on LJ Speech (public domain), LibriTTS-R (CC BY 4.0) and VCTK (CC BY 4.0).
synthetic_privacy.privacy_notice: Every name, number, address, credential and document identifier is fictional. Telephone numbers use the NANP 555-01xx fictional range and web/e-mail addresses use the RFC 2606 reserved example domains. No real personal information is present.

public.name: LibriSpeech dev-clean subset
public.upstream: LibriSpeech ASR corpus, dev-clean validation split
public.citation: V. Panayotov, G. Chen, D. Povey and S. Khudanpur, "Librispeech: An ASR corpus based on public domain audio books", ICASSP 2015, pp. 5206-5210.
public.selection: Round-robin over duration buckets, shortest first within each bucket, corpus sorted by utterance id. No randomness.
public.privacy_notice: Not annotated for private information and excluded from every privacy metric. Read prose contains person names, so the model detects real entities here that carry no gold annotation.
